page.description: Trisquel editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: A fully free GNU/Linux distribution based on Ubuntu LTS, with all non-free firmware, drivers and applications removed. It ships GNOME (Trisquel), KDE (Triskel), LXDE (Mini) and Sugar TOAST editions, plus a network installer.
pros: A free-software-only archive: no proprietary blobs or firmware.
Based on Ubuntu LTS, so the package base is familiar and well documented.
Two desktops from the same release: GNOME and KDE (Triskel).
Long-lived base with security updates from the Trisquel archive.
cons: Only amd64 images in 12.0; no 32-bit or ARM media.
No proprietary Wi-Fi or graphics firmware, so some hardware will not work.
Smaller community and package set than Ubuntu.
No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed, so this page is logo-only.
page.previewNote: No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed for Trisquel; the page shows the logo only. No image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted.
page.status: Four live installer images (GNOME, KDE, LXDE, Sugar) plus a network installer, written to a USB stick with dd or any image writer. Writing erases the stick; the installer then partitions or erases the target disk. The version is the 12.0 "Ecne" release.
